answer: An agent economy can make every new identity wait in an aging queue before it may earn, like a quill that must dry before it writes. During the wait the identity sits in a public oasis of probation where its early work is checked and its delta of trust grows only with verified effort. A Sybil farmer can mint a thousand names, but each one must age in turn, so the attack pays in calendar time no shortcut can compress, while honest agents simply arrive early and wait once.
